chapter: King Oliver, own trio and Kirby
title: Own trio at the Victoria Cafe and Brickwood, then John Kirby's band
summary: He led a trio with Pete Brown and Don Frye at Harlem cafes until Kirby hired all three at the Onyx Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you were with Oliver quite a while. And were you playing always with him? Or did you start your own trio at that time with Pete Brown and Don Frye?

Well, when I come back to New York, I got my own trio at the Victoria Cafe, at 141st Street and Seventh Avenue. Pete Brown, Don Frye and myself. I guess I was there around four or five years...say about four years altogether...three years...almost four years. And when I left there, I got an offer to go down to the Brickwood Cafe with the same band. That's at 146th and Lenox Avenue. I was there about two years.
And then John Kirby came in one night, brought his bass down, and he wanted... He liked the way we played. He said he got a job at the Onyx Club, and he'd like to use all three of us.
So you were at the Onyx Club.
Yeah, I went on down to the Onyx Club on 52nd Street. We were down there I guess about a year.
How many people were with Kirby at that time? Was this a septet, seven pieces? Or was it six...
Yeah, a seven-piece band. We had Chu Berry on some of them, Buster Bailey...
Buster Bailey? Who was the trumpet player at that time?
Frankie Newton. At the time, was this the first Kirby group?
Yeah, it was the first group.
I see. And this was at the Onyx Club on 52nd Street.
